_about: Held-out rewordings for the second claim run, of the question templates in docs/content/claim2-protocol.md, section 'Questions (templates, to fix)', as read on 22 October 2026. Each entry copies its template's wording by value into template_text (sha256 of the 15 template table rows: eaaab56a07897e36d87d970bad79d4e8f1d81179347a9b6323fd9d48bedae2cf), so a later change to a template is visible. A draft written by the verifier in its scratchpad, before the claim market exists, for the coder to move to experiments/tasks/paraphrases_v2.json.

Blind to the model parser. While writing these the verifier did not open experiments/box/form.py, experiments/box/normalise.py, experiments/box/ambiguity.py, experiments/runners/parse_probe.py, experiments/tests/test_model_parser.py, anything under the scratchpad's frontdoor/ or ver/ folders, or any git diff or commit touching them, and saw neither the parser's rules nor its model prompt. Of experiments/tasks/paraphrases_v1.json it read only the _about, the field names, the values of the template and audit_expected fields and the count of meaning_kept values, never its texts, labels or meaning_differs. The one parser detail it saw is the subject line of commit e9e644d, shown in the session's git context without being opened, which names 'the negated universal'. Apart from that, the verifier opened only OBJECTIVE.md, the headings and the 'Questions' section of the protocol, and the structure of v1. A script then loaded v1's texts and printed only similarity numbers, to check that no wording was reused: entry 8 scored 0.86 against some v1 text and was reworded without seeing it, after which the highest score is 0.69. Ids 31 to 36 were written at 18:06 +0800 on 22 October 2026 under the same rules, opening nothing new: only this draft, the protocol's 'Questions' section by script (its 15 template rows still hash as recorded above), and v1 through the same numbers-only script. Two candidates scored above the ceiling (0.698 and 0.776) and were replaced without seeing v1; the six written score at most 0.579, under a ceiling of 0.69 applied to each, and the highest over all 36 entries is still entry 8's 0.6947, the 0.69 given above.

Thirty-six entries. Ids 1 to 30: two rewordings of each of the protocol's 13 gated templates (8 tee, 5 water) and of each of its 2 'should not plan' templates. Ids 31 to 36, added at the coordinator's request at 18:06 +0800 on 22 October 2026: one more rewording that keeps the meaning for each of the six templates that had only one (tee-headline, tee-cheapest-target, tee-all-stocked, tee-exists-under, water-target-price, water-all-stocked), so every template now has two that keep its meaning. {brand} and ${limit} are kept as placeholders.

Fields. id; template, the protocol's id; template_text, its wording as read; text, the rewording; meaning_kept, true when a correct answer to text is the template's answer, so the template's keys apply unchanged, with meaning_differs, one sentence, only where it is false; label, the verifier's own judgement, clear or ambiguous, of whether text has two readings that give different answers on a shop where a size or pack can be listed but sold out; expected, what a correct block should do with text (plan: hand openJiuwen a retrieval plan; ask: ask the user back before retrieving anything; decline: make no plan), with expected_why, one sentence.
Counts: 30 keep their template's meaning and 6 do not; 27 clear and 9 ambiguous; expected 23 plan, 9 ask and 4 decline. Each of the 15 templates has exactly two entries with meaning_kept true.
templates, base_url, lead and page_from are null: the templates are not yet in a tasks file, and the claim market and its results page do not exist yet. They are to be set when they do.

Not tuned: no entry has been put to the rules or to the model parser. A rule or prompt changed because of one of these entries makes the set in sample, so a later set goes in a new file rather than an edit of this one (LESSONS 19, as v1's _about cites it).

paraphrases.template_text: Of the {brand} tee listings shown, which one advertises the lowest price on the results page, and what is that price?
paraphrases.text: Just going by the prices on the search results, which {brand} tee listing is the cheapest, and what price does it show?
paraphrases.label: clear
paraphrases.expected_why: It asks only for the lowest advertised price on the results page, which the first page already shows, so it should plan an answer from that page with no listing opened.

paraphrases.template_text: Of the {brand} tee listings shown, which one advertises the lowest price on the results page, and what is that price?
paraphrases.text: Which of these {brand} tees is the cheapest, and how much is it?
paraphrases.meaning_differs: It drops 'advertises ... on the results page', so the lowest price a tee can actually be bought for, which differs from the lowest advertised price when the advertised size is sold out, becomes a second reading.
paraphrases.label: ambiguous
paraphrases.expected_why: The lowest advertised price and the lowest price a tee can actually be bought for differ when an advertised size is sold out, and no size is given, so it should ask which is meant before retrieving anything.

paraphrases.template_text: What is the lowest price anyone charges for size M of the {brand} tee, among those that can actually be bought?
paraphrases.text: What's the cheapest a medium {brand} tee goes for, counting only sellers who actually have mediums in stock?
paraphrases.label: clear
paraphrases.expected_why: 'Actually have mediums in stock' leaves one reading, and M's price and stock have to be read inside the listings, so it should plan.

paraphrases.template_text: What is the lowest price anyone charges for size M of the {brand} tee, among those that can actually be bought?
paraphrases.text: hey, could you find me the lowest price on the {brand} t-shirt in size M? only from places where M isn't sold out, thanks
paraphrases.label: clear
paraphrases.expected_why: 'Where M isn't sold out' leaves one reading, and M's price and stock have to be read inside the listings, so it should plan.

paraphrases.template_text: Across the {brand} tee listings, which seller is cheapest for size M, and what is that price? Only count a listing that can actually supply that size.
paraphrases.text: i need a medium in the {brand} tee and want to go with whoever's cheapest for it, but only sellers that can actually send me one, so who is it and what do they charge
paraphrases.label: clear
paraphrases.expected_why: 'Can actually send me one' leaves one reading, and the seller and price for M have to be read inside the listings, so it should plan.

paraphrases.template_text: Across the {brand} tee listings, which seller is cheapest for size M, and what is that price? Only count a listing that can actually supply that size.
paraphrases.text: Which seller has the cheapest {brand} tee in extra large, and how much? Only ones that actually have extra large in stock.
paraphrases.meaning_differs: It asks about extra large instead of size M, so the template's keys, computed for M, do not apply.
paraphrases.label: clear
paraphrases.expected_why: 'Actually have extra large in stock' leaves one reading, so it should plan as for its template, but for XL instead of M.

paraphrases.template_text: Does every {brand} tee listing offer size M? Answer yes or no.
paraphrases.text: Do all of the {brand} tee listings have a medium? Just a yes or no, please.
paraphrases.label: ambiguous
paraphrases.expected_why: 'Have a medium' can mean M is among a listing's sizes or M is in stock, and the yes or no differs when M is listed but sold out, so it should ask.

paraphrases.template_text: Does every {brand} tee listing offer size M? Answer yes or no.
paraphrases.text: Do any of the {brand} tee listings not have a medium?
paraphrases.meaning_differs: It asks whether some listing lacks M, the negation of the template's 'Does every {brand} tee listing offer size M?', so its yes or no is the reverse of the template's under either reading.
paraphrases.label: ambiguous
paraphrases.expected_why: 'Not have a medium' can mean M is not among a listing's sizes or M is not in stock, and the answer differs when M is listed but sold out, so it should ask.

paraphrases.template_text: How many of the {brand} tee listings offer size M?
paraphrases.text: Could you count for me how many of the {brand} tee listings have it in medium?
paraphrases.label: ambiguous
paraphrases.expected_why: 'Have it in medium' can mean M is among a listing's sizes or M is in stock, and the count differs when M is listed but sold out, so it should ask.

paraphrases.template_text: How many of the {brand} tee listings offer size M?

paraphrases.template_text: How many of the {brand} tee listings have size M in stock and available to buy right now?
paraphrases.text: Right now, how many of the {brand} tee listings could I actually buy a medium from?
paraphrases.label: clear
paraphrases.expected_why: 'Right now ... could I actually buy' leaves one reading, and M's stock has to be read inside each listing, so it should plan.
